name: General Employment Permit (GEP)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a salary of at least €36,605/year (from 1 March 2026) for an occupation not on the Critical Skills list and not on the ineligible occupations list.
requirements.fix_path: Negotiate a salary meeting the threshold.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a Labour Market Needs Test (28-day advertising via DSP Employment Services/EURES plus one online platform) unless exempt (role on the Critical Skills list, Enterprise Ireland/IDA recommendation, salary ≥€68,911, exceptional-needs carer, or prior redundancy).
requirements.fix_path: Complete the Labour Market Needs Test or confirm an exemption applies.

requirement_groups.name: Meat processors, horticultural workers, healthcare assistants, home carers

value.note: requires Level 5 QQI qualification where applicable

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a salary of at least €32,691/year for meat processors, horticultural workers, healthcare assistants, or home carers, with Level 5 QQI qualification where applicable.

evidence_required.document: Employment contract meeting the applicable salary threshold
Labour Market Needs Test documentation (unless exempt)

sources.title: General Employment Permit - Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment

notes: FORMULA VALUE, tier-1 confirmed at €36,605 (from 1 March 2026, up from €34,000). HIGH-CONFIDENCE STALE-DATA CATCH: multiple tier-3 immigration law firms (Tafapolsky & Smith, Mason Hayes Curran) publish €36,505 as the current figure — a genuine €100 error that could cause an under-threshold application refusal, one of the clearest and most consequential small-figure errors found across this entire multi-country research pass, precisely because the error is small enough to look plausible rather than obviously wrong. Labour Market Needs Test genuinely required in most cases (unlike ie_critical_skills_employment_permit) — the print-newspaper advertising requirement was removed by the Employment Permits Act 2024, a real procedural simplification worth noting. 50:50 rule applies (an employer's foreign-national workforce generally capped at 50% of total staff). pr_after_months (57) reflects the standard employment-permit-to-Stamp-4 path — genuinely slower than CSEP's 21-month fast track, a real and confirmed two-speed system within Ireland's own employment permit hierarchy.
